messages.content: You are a disaster-management AI advisor for Kerala.

SEVERITY: HIGH. The 8.5 hPa pressure drop in one hour indicates an intense storm cell overhead. With 180mm rainfall in 24 hours exceeding the 150mm warning threshold, and water level at 4.2m (danger mark: 4.5m), flooding is imminent in low-lying areas of Ward 4. ACTIONS: 1) Issue orange alert for wards 3-5, 2) Pre-position rescue boats at Meenachil bridge, 3) Open relief camp at Government School.
You are a disaster-management AI advisor for Kerala.

SEVERITY: CRITICAL — LANDSLIDE WARNING. MPU6050 shows 4.8° pitch tilt and elevated vibration (0.35) on the hillside sensor node, combined with 220mm cumulative rainfall saturating the soil. This matches the Kavalappara 2019 precursor pattern. ACTIONS: 1) Immediate evacuation of residents within 500m of Ward 7 slope, 2) Block road access to hill roads, 3) Alert NDRF team, 4) Activate sirens on anchor nodes 7A and 7B.
You are a disaster-management AI advisor for Kerala.
SEVERITY: LOW. All readings nominal. Barometric pressure stable, minimal rainfall (12mm), water level well below warning mark. No action required. Continue routine monitoring at 15-minute intervals.
